messages:
Samira: incident-bot reports: [ALERT] elevated 5xx rate from eu-west-1 ELB clusters — apparent connection resets and target deregistrations. paging oncall.
incident-bot: INCIDENT OPENED: #INC-2026-2187654321 - eu-west-1 networking/serving degradation (ELB health flaps + Route53 slow failover). Severity: P1. Pager duty: Samira.
Samira: I'm on it. seeing spike in 502/504s from edge -> elb -> app. dashboards show ELB target group health toggling for two autoscaling groups in az-a and az-b.
Diego: pulling logs. ELB logs show `target: deregistration` and `connection_reset` around the same time as EBS io latency errors on several instances. looks like kernel I/O wait -> app thread starvation -> healthcheck fail.
Liam: Confirmed from metrics: EBS read latency > 200ms for several EBS volumes attached to asg-eu-west-1a. ASG noticed increased unhealthy targets and started draining instances which made ELB immediately shift traffic. Route53 health checks are still evaluating, TTL 60s — but resolver caches in some CDNs/ISPs are sticking to stale records and sending to the impacted AZs -> partial customer impact.
Nora: Customer reports: 2 enterprise customers intermittently saw 40-60% error rates for calls routed to eu-west-1. Other regions fine. Need mitigation plan: 1) stop draining so ASG doesn't churn, 2) reduce Route53 healthcheck reliance, 3) shift traffic away from the problematic AZs.
Samira: Actions in progress: 1) paused ASG scale-in and suspended the termination process for the two ASGs (`aws autoscaling suspend-processes --auto-scaling-group-name <name> --scaling-processes Terminate`). 2) raised team on EBS: tagging storage as suspect and snapshotting.
ops-bot: runbook step 1: increase ELB deregistration timeout to 300s to avoid rapid re-registration flapping. Command: `aws elbv2 modify-target-group --target-group-arn <arn> --deregistration-delay-timeout-seconds 300`
Diego: doing the ELB tweak now. also bumping NLB idle timeout for edge proxies to 120s to reduce resets. applying to both regional ELBs.
Samira: Next: Route53 failover — health checks are tied to ALB endpoints. We should create a temporary weighted record to shift 90% traffic to eu-west-2 and 10% to eu-west-1 (for slow validation), then promote once stable. Lower Route53 TTL to 15s to speed up propagation.
Liam: I can create the weighted policy. Will set weight: eu-west-2=90, eu-west-1=10 and change health-check config TTL=15. Executing now. Note: some resolvers ignore TTL but most will respect it.
incident-bot: ACTION LOGGED: weight change initiated by Liam at ts=2187654350.
Nora: Customer comms: drafting an in-product banner and status page blurb. ETA 10m. Anything to call out? severity and which customers impacted.
Samira: include: 'intermittent API errors in eu-west-1, partial traffic routed to eu-west-1 for some customers. Mitigation: traffic shifting and storage investigation. No data loss reported.'
Avery: Quick question — do we have cross-region read-replicas for the affected storage? If not, snapshot+restore could be slow. Also, we should check if kernels on instances have I/O scheduler misconfig after recent AMI update.
Diego: Good catch. AMI build 2026.03.01 had a kernel bump that changed io scheduler defaults. I'm checking AMI in eu-west-1. Instances with high io latency are on that AMI.
Samira: Handoff to second on-call: Liam, I'm going to step out for an urgent customer call in 8m. Can you take over the coordination? I'll leave the ELB and Route53 changes in a safe state.
Liam: Taking over. Samira — please post a quick summary before you drop. I'll run the paging rotation and coordinate with storage.
Samira: Summary: EBS io latency spike + kernel/AMI changes likely cause; ELB target flapping; Route53 TTL=60 causing slow failover for cached resolvers; actions: paused ASG termination, increased ELB deregistration to 300s, set Route53 weighted record to route 90% to eu-west-2, lowered TTL to 15s, snapshotting volumes. No data integrity issues detected. Handoff: Liam.
Samira: :wave: off to call. @Liam you're owner.
Liam: Acknowledged. Next steps I'll run: - monitor ELB target stability for 15m - verify error rate in eu-west-2 falls to baseline - coordinate with storage team for EBS snapshot completion and AMI kernel revert plan.
ops-bot: runbook step 3: if error rate > 10% after traffic shift, enable cross-region failover to eu-west-2 (route53 set weight 100). Use `aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id <zone> --change-batch file://shift-to-euw2.json`
Diego: ELB logs post-deregistration-delay change show fewer flaps. EBS snapshots started. Error rate in eu-west-2 already down by 85%.
Liam: I'm going to keep the weighted record for 30m and watch. If stable, we'll cut to 100% eu-west-2 and then begin recovery steps for eu-west-1.
Nora: Customer comms posted to status: "Intermittent errors in eu-west-1; traffic being rerouted to eu-west-2; impacts likely for small fraction of requests. Engineers actively mitigating." Added link to internal status updates and support runbook. :lock:
incident-bot: NOTE: On-call handoff recorded. Previous owner: Samira. New owner: Liam.
Diego: Quick log snippet for postmortem: ```ELB-Log: target_status=UNHEALTHY reason=Target.Deregistration; kernel: blk_mq: mq_run_hctx_timeout on nvme1n1; dmesg: md: I/O error```
Liam: Good. I'll schedule a follow-up postmortem and tag infra/storage/ami teams. For now keeping weighted routing in place and ASG suspended. If any partner customers request an override, escalate to SEPs.
Nora: Any estimates on time to full restore for eu-west-1? if we need to rebuild instances with prior AMI, that could be ~45-60m for full roll.
Diego: Snapshot+restore + AMI bake + deploy ~40-70m. But we can restore traffic to eu-west-1 in read-only or low-traffic mode sooner once we confirm storage stability.
Liam: Plan: 30m watch window. If error rate <2% for 30m, cut weight to 100% eu-west-2 and start scheduled recovery for eu-west-1. Postmortem owner: Diego.
Samira: Thanks team. leaving final notes on the incident doc. I'll join the postmortem. :heart:
ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Reduced customer impact. Traffic shifted; storage snapshots in progress; ASG termination suspended; on-call: Liam. Incident will remain P1 until eu-west-1 fully validated / traffic restored.
Liam: closing loop for now — monitoring and running alerts. Will update thread with cutover time or rollback. If anyone sees any regression ping me directly.
